findings.title: Grant-type matcher checks the wrong characters and reverses the comparison
findings.body: The encoded grant shortcut occupies indexes 4 and 5, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5), and returns false when that substring equals the expected value rather than when it differs. Consequently, an ID such as 'onrtna:<uuid>' passes an authorization-code expectation of 'ac', so the updated integration assertions do not detect missing or incorrect grant context. Validate the prefix length and reject when substring(4, 6) does not equal the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Shortcut contract permits values the encoder cannot decode
findings.body: The new factory contract recommends a three-letter shortcut, while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context prefix composed of three two-character shortcuts. The factory accepts longer shortcuts without validation and encodeTokenId emits them, so a custom grant implementing the documented three-letter shortcut produces token IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId immediately rejects. Specify exactly two characters in the contract and validate that requirement when registering grant shortcuts.
